reasoning_traces.think:
The three primitives form a coherent analytical triad: defensive efficiency ranking captures static team resilience, quarterback aggressiveness index reflects dynamic offensive risk-taking, and personnel shift impact models adaptive strategic evolution. These operators are mathematically grounded in time-series ranking and difference-in-differences frameworks. The first primitive maps penalty frequency to expected points, assuming uniform distribution of penalties. The second uses ratio-based normalization to quantify aggression, relying on consistent play categorization. The third applies temporal differencing to isolate strategic effect, assuming baseline stability. Failure modes include misclassification of penalties, inconsistent data labeling, and spurious correlation due to omitted variables. Dualities emerge in how each metric can be interpreted both descriptively and normatively—e.g., high aggressiveness may correlate with high variance but not necessarily success. The epistemic structure supports causal inference through observational data, with each primitive serving as a node in a Bayesian network of team performance.
